raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The AMD nightly `nightly-1-gpu-zimage-turbo` has failed on all three ROCm variants since the 2026-09-21 run ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35633070401/job/106443720276)), and was still failing on 2026-10-12:

```
PerformanceValidationError: [performance] zimage_image_t2i: Load duration missing or invalid: None
```

Image generation succeeds; the failure is in recording the result. #39206 added a `load_time_ms=None` parameter to `DiffusionServerBase._validate_and_record`, and a check in `_record_performance_result` that rejects a missing load duration, but only updated the base class's own call site. Three tests override `test_diffusion_generation` and call `_validate_and_record(case, perf_record)` directly, so they record `None` even though the server measured its load time:

- `test/registered/amd/test_zimage_turbo.py`
- `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_zimage_turbo.py`
- `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`

## Modifications

`_validate_and_record` now takes the `ServerContext` and reads `ctx.load_time_ms` itself, as `_validate_realtime_performance` already does. The three overrides, the base-class call site and `test_performance_failure_policy.py` pass the context. Since `ctx` is required, an override still using the old call fails with a `TypeError` instead of silently recording `None`.

NVIDIA behaviour is unchanged: the base class used to pass `diffusion_server.load_time_ms` and now passes `diffusion_server`.

## Verification

- The NVIDIA diffusion suites (1/2/4-GPU, 5090, `diffusion-coverage-check`) and `multimodal-gen-unit-test` passed on this branch at e9616a3e ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38293317709)).
- The AMD zimage nightly, dispatched on this branch at c1e4114d with `continue_on_error=false` ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38473414064)), passes on rocm10, rocm724 and rocm720. Each job records the server's load time (52.3–58.6 s) instead of failing on `None`.

An earlier revision also added a guard test that drove the three overrides with a stub server. It has been removed: with `ctx` required, it no longer catches anything the signature doesn't.

## Notes for reviewers

Two XPU issues are left alone because this regression did not cause them:

- The XPU nightlies error during fixture setup with `fixture 'perf_results' not found`. `test/registered/amd/conftest.py` re-exports it (#38686), but `test/registered/xpu/` has no equivalent.
- `flux2_dev_image_t2i` has no entry in `perf_baselines/xpu_b60.json`, so once the fixture is fixed it will fail on the missing baseline (#39206 moved that check out of `if case.run_perf_check:`).

<!-- pr-states:start -->
---
### CI States

Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #38519229876](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519229876)<!-- slot:pr-test:end -->
Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #38519229934](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519229934)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:x: [Run #38519229845](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38519229845)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end -->
<!-- pr-states:end -->

nodes.body:
Superseding my two earlier comments — both name runs that later pushes made stale. **Do not rerun 35677085181 or 35684596604.**

Current head is `dc90df43`. Its `pr-test.yml` run is [35692466008](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35692466008); once it finishes, the action needed is a failed-jobs-only rerun of *that* run (`/rerun-failed-ci`, or `gh run rerun 35692466008 --failed --repo sgl-project/sglang`). It is still finishing only because GPU runners are contended — the remaining jobs fail-fast the moment a runner picks them up.

## This change is green

- `Lint` — success on `dc90df43`.
- `call-multimodal-gen-tests / multimodal-gen-unit-test` — success, on this head and the previous one. That is the suite carrying the new guard, and it executed for real rather than being collected-and-skipped: all three overrides driven, each recording `load=44977.73ms`.
- `multimodal-gen-test-1-5090`, `bcg-diffusion`, `compute-diffusion-partitions` and all ten `base-a-test-cpu` shards — success.
- On the earlier head `a3f865da`, where the 1-GPU diffusion suite got to complete before fail-fast, `diffusion-coverage-check` reported **45 of 45 cases executed, 45 passed, 0 failed**. Those all drive `_validate_and_record` through the base class against a real server.

## Everything red is one root cause

Every other failed job in the run emits this in its own log:

```
Fail-fast: skipping — root cause job(s): call-multimodal-gen-tests / multimodal-gen-test-1-b200
```

I checked all twenty individually. `wait-for-base-b` is a cascade of a cascade, and `diffusion-coverage-check` fails only because the 2-GPU suite was cut before running.

## That root cause is flaky on `main`, not caused by this PR

Worth flagging to the diffusion owners, since it makes the b200 lane a coin flip for any PR touching `multimodal_gen`.

The last scheduled `main` run's b200 job ([106570862025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35666291374)) failed the same nvfp4 cases and went green only on its fourth retry:

```
attempt 1: 2 failed, 3 passed
attempt 2: 2 failed, 3 deselected
attempt 3: 1 failed, 1 passed, 3 deselected
attempt 4: 1 passed, 4 deselected
```

On that `main` run, `flux1_modelopt_nvfp4_t2i` measured `e2e=1612.05ms` against `expected_e2e_ms=836.71` with a `1045.89ms` limit — `main` is ~1.9x over its own threshold on that case. My runs measured 1424–1925ms for the same test, i.e. the same range. `qwen_image_2512_modelopt_nvfp4_t2i` is similar, measuring 18.5–37.9s against a `9650.06ms` baseline.

So the outcome is decided by which retry happens to draw a fast enough sample within the 7-attempt budget. `main` drew one; these runs did not. It is also not reachable from this diff: `validate_e2e` reads `summary.e2e_ms` from `collect_metrics(perf_record)`, which this PR does not touch, and on the base-class path the change is behaviourally identical — it previously passed `diffusion_server.load_time_ms` as an argument and now reads `ctx.load_time_ms` off the same object.

Those baselines look due a re-seed, but that is a separate change in a lane this PR does not own, and I have deliberately not touched them — widening a perf gate that happens to be blocking my own PR would be the wrong fix for the wrong reason.

@michaelzhang-ai heads-up — this PR now conflicts with `main` (`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`) as of `fb746818`, so CI cannot run to completion.

Could you merge or rebase `main` into `cursor/fix-diffusion-load-time-regression-1b8e`? Happy to help if the conflict lands in AMD/ROCm code.

@yichiche Two updates since your approval:

- I dropped the guard test (`test/registered/unit/diffusion/test_diffusion_server_load_time_recording.py`). With `ctx` now a required argument, an override using the old call fails with a `TypeError`, so the test no longer caught anything extra. The PR is down to the five call-site and signature changes.
- I dispatched the AMD zimage nightly on this branch at c1e4114d with `continue_on_error=false`: [run 38473414064](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38473414064). `zimage_image_t2i` passes on rocm10, rocm724 and rocm720, and each job records the load time (52.3–58.6 s) instead of failing on `None`.

The NVIDIA `base-b` jobs are being rerun after GitHub API 502s in the fail-fast step; no tests had run in those jobs.
PR 40657 passes pre-review: the diffusion test helper reads the load duration from the server context, NVIDIA still records the same load_time_ms, and every checklist row passed. LGTM.

@@ -390,12 +390,17 @@ def run_and_collect(
 
     def _validate_and_record(
         self,
+        ctx: ServerContext,
         case: DiffusionTestCase,
         perf_record: RequestPerfRecord,
         request_index: int = 1,
-        load_time_ms: float | None = None,
     ) -> None:
-        """Validate metrics and record results."""
+        """Validate metrics and record results.
+
+        The load duration is read off ``ctx`` rather than passed separately:
+        recording a result requires it, and a caller that has the server always
+        has the measurement.
+        """
         if perf_record is None:
             raise PerformanceValidationError(
                 f"[performance] {case.id}: request performance record is missing"

         )
 
         summary = validator.collect_metrics(perf_record)
-        summary.load_time_ms = load_time_ms
+        summary.load_time_ms = ctx.load_time_ms
         self._record_performance_result(case, summary, request_index)
         self._print_performance_log(case, summary, scenario)
 
@@ -1727,7 +1732,7 @@ def run_case_check(name: str, fn: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
             run_case_check(
                 "performance",
                 lambda: self._validate_and_record(
-                    case, perf_record, request_index, diffusion_server.load_time_ms
+                    diffusion_server, case, perf_record, request_index
                 ),
             )

@@ -3,6 +3,7 @@

     )
-    server._validate_and_record(case, record, load_time_ms=100)

     assert len(server._perf_results) == 1
